SELECT 
  fished_date_doy,
  fished_date_season,
  cls,
  COUNT(*) as trips,
  ROUND(AVG(yt), 2) as avg_yt,
  ROUND(AVG(anglers), 0) as avg_anglers,
  ROUND(SUM(yt) / (SUM(anglers) + COUNT(*)), 3) as share_approx
FROM trips
WHERE fished_date_doy >= 240 AND fished_date_doy <= 305
  AND fished_date_season IN (2, 3, 4, 5)
GROUP BY fished_date_doy, fished_date_season, cls
ORDER BY fished_date_season, fished_date_doy, cls
LIMIT 100;

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Aggregate all trips by season and doy to understand the seasonal pattern
trips = tables['trips']

# Filter for September-October (doy 240-305)
sep_oct = trips[(trips['fished_date_doy'] >= 240) & (trips['fished_date_doy'] <= 305)]

# Calculate share per trip: yt / (anglers + competitors on same boat/class/date)
# Group by fished_date_t to count competitors
trip_summary = []
for (season, doy, cls), group in sep_oct.groupby(['fished_date_season', 'fished_date_doy', 'cls']):
    total_yt = group['yt'].sum()
    total_anglers = group['anglers'].sum()
    num_trips = len(group)
    # Approximate share as if one angler per boat (to show raw yt/angler potential)
    share = total_yt / (total_anglers + num_trips) if (total_anglers + num_trips) > 0 else 0
    trip_summary.append({
        'season': season,
        'doy': doy,
        'cls': cls,
        'trips': num_trips,
        'yt': total_yt,
        'anglers': total_anglers,
        'share': share,
        'avg_yt': total_yt / num_trips if num_trips > 0 else 0
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(trip_summary)

# Group by season and doy, take max share to highlight best classes
best_by_day = df.groupby(['season', 'doy']).agg({
    'share': 'max',
    'cls': lambda x: df.loc[df['share'] == df.loc[x.index, 'share'].max(), 'cls'].iloc[0],
    'trips': 'sum'
}).reset_index()
best_by_day.columns = ['season', 'doy', 'best_share', 'best_class', 'total_trips']

# Show the pattern
print("September-October peaks by season (doy 240-305):")
print(best_by_day[best_by_day['best_share'] > 0.2].sort_values(['season', 'doy']))

# Find the peak days by season
print("\nTop 10 peak days across all seasons:")
print(df[df['share'] > 0.3].sort_values('share', ascending=False).head(10))
